issues.description: The solution for Aufgabe 04 uses a column alias (regierungsbezirk AS District) while the problem statement explicitly instructs students not to rename columns with AS unless asked. This creates a cross-artifact inconsistency: the solution demonstrates a practice the instructions prohibit and may confuse students about whether using AS is allowed.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent: either remove the alias from the solution (use SELECT regierungsbezirk, SUM(einwohner_w), SUM(einwohner_m) ...) so it follows the instruction not to rename columns, or update the problem statement to permit using AS where appropriate. Prefer removing the alias in the solution to preserve the current instruction.

issues.description: The solution for Aufgabe 04 renames the column regierungsbezirk to the English alias District (SELECT regierungsbezirk AS District). The problem statement and instructions use the German term 'Regierungsbezirk' and explicitly advise not to rename columns with AS when not requested. Presenting the district column under a different name ('District') creates an unnecessary naming mismatch between the problem description and the solution output and may confuse students mapping the requirement (Regierungsbezirk) to the query result.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the alias and output the original column name used in the schema. Use SELECT regierungsbezirk, SUM(einwohner_w), SUM(einwohner_m) ... GROUP BY regierungsbezirk so the column name in the result matches the problem wording ('Regierungsbezirk'). If an alias is required, alias to the same German identifier (AS regierungsbezirk) rather than 'District'.
